1.explanation:
1. We pass defaultValue (via useState) including a timezone offset ("-08:00"), so internally the component normalizes it to UTC and ends up with a June 30 date when displaying the calendar.  
2. We supply calendarProps.bounds as date-only strings for July 1 and July 31. Those strings are parsed as local-midnight dates. Because of the shift from the timezone offset, June 30 falls within the parsed UTC numeric range.  
3. The result is that the June 30 cell remains enabled and selectable even though the visible month is outside our specified July bounds, reproducing the bug shown in the screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: In our example we set the DateInput bounds to only allow dates between 2020-07-01 and 2020-07-31, but because we passed in a defaultValue string that includes a timezone offset ("2020-07-02T00:00:00-08:00"), the calendar internally shifts that into UTC and ends up showing June 2020. As a result, the June 30 tile (the last day of the previous month) is still rendered as enabled and even selectable, even though it lies outside of our specified bounds.
